title: Module and local Hom transport under a ringed-topos equivalence
statement: Let $e:(\mathscr X,R)\to(\mathscr X',R')$ be an equivalence of ringed topoi presented by small sites [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]: its underlying geometric morphism is an equivalence and $e^{-1}R'\to R$ is an isomorphism. The module adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] is an exact equivalence $e^*\dashv e_*$ of module-sheaf categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Termwise application gives mutually inverse equivalences of unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], preserving K-injective complexes [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. For every sheaf of sets $V'$ in $\mathscr X'$, the induced equivalence on the slice topoi over $V'$ and $e^{-1}V'$ has these same properties for the restricted rings. Slice over a site object means slice over its sheafified representable [lem-weil-pbc-localized-sheaves-over-representable]. These equivalences commute with further restrictions, derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and localization of the restricted ring at a section [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization]. For an ideal subsheaf $\mathcal I'\subset R'$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-ideal-generators], put $\mathcal I=e^*\mathcal I'$. Then the tests $R\mathcal Hom(R'|_{V'}[1/a],N|_{V'})=0$ for all site objects $V'$ and $a\in\mathcal I'(V')$ hold if and only if the tests $R\mathcal Hom(R|_V[1/b],e^*N|_V)=0$ hold for all site objects $V$ of the other presentation and $b\in\mathcal I(V)$.
